title: Choose the visual world for 3D Print OS
question: The roll assigned the T-Card Planning Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: T-Card Planning Board
options.lineage: Steel T-card racks on workshop walls: one coloured card per job, slotted by machine and moved as work progresses
options.thesis: Every job is a coloured card in a rack; its colour is its status, its slot is its printer.
options.viewport: Steel-blue rail with Sales / Production / Business; dashboard leads with the live rack: one slot column per printer, each job a card with a coloured tab head, grams, hours and price in tabular figures; quotes and orders tables carry the same card-tab colour on every row.
options.risk: Five card colours plus state colours can turn into confetti unless each colour means exactly one status.

raised.raise: One type size carries every table; rank comes from position and card colour, never from size jumps.
Card stocks are flat, unmodulated fills: no gradients, no grain, no shadow under a card.
The printer fleet is a fixed, finite roster: every printer keeps its slot even when idle.

options.label: Job Traveler
options.lineage: Machine-shop routing sheets that travel with a part from quote to shipping, stamped at each operation
options.thesis: Every order is a traveler: a sheet of operations stamped off one by one.
options.viewport: Dark slate top bar; orders list where each row shows its routing as a strip of operation boxes (Slice · Print · QC · Pack) stamped as done.
options.risk: Manila card stock drifts toward the warm-cream default; must stay cool and strict to avoid nostalgia.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: The production queue as a departures board: jobs are departures, printers are platforms.
options.viewport: Black ground; queue table in fixed character columns (Job · Printer · Start · ETA · Status), delayed jobs lit amber, failed in red.
options.case: Fuses cleanly on the queue and printers; reads less natural on pricing and settings forms. Holds clarity, loses identification.
options.risk: Becomes a costume of a board on screens that are forms, not schedules.

options.label: Graphite Console
options.thesis: A graphite workbench of persistent panels split by one-pixel seams.
options.viewport: Persistent three-panel layout: nav, queue list, selected job detail with slice breakdown.
options.case: Very clear, but any SaaS could ship it; print shops don't see themselves in it.
options.risk: Generic dark dashboard; dark-only hurts the shop-floor phone in daylight.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Sections as coloured divider boards under clear acetate leaves.
options.case: A reading world; staff are operating, not reading.
options.risk: Serif body at 17px is wrong for dense tables.
options.kept: One size does the work: hierarchy by position, not size.

options.label: Guide Map Lobes
options.thesis: Areas as swelling lobes of flat colour.
options.case: Lobes fight tables; no fit for an operations tool.
options.risk: Playful to the point of distrust on prices.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Magnitude as dot size on a navy chart.
options.case: No link to print shops; data isn't spatial.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.kept: A finite roster where every member keeps its place.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean white SaaS console with one indigo accent, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, greeting, four stat tiles, revenue chart and recent quotes.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other admin panel by design; it is close to what ships today.
